subject: art
title: Invigilated Practical Examination
keyDates: Window: three days set by the SEC each year. 2026 was Tuesday 21, Wednesday 22 and Thursday 23 April 2026. The 2027 dates are not yet published
Held shortly after the coursework period ends. Your teacher tells you your day
Length: 5 hours in one day, in two periods of 2.5 hours with a break between (2026 brief)
After the exam your Visual Journal, Artefact A and Artefact B are sealed and held in school until the SEC examiner marks them in June
summary: The Invigilated Practical Examination is 20% of Art, marked out of 100. In 5 hours on one day, split into two 2.5 hour periods, you make Artefact B from scratch, using the development work in your Visual Journal. Examiners mark the finished Artefact B on criteria F to J, using the same common brief and bands as the coursework. Ordinary Level marks are converted from a common reference scale.

stages.name: Plan Artefact B in your journal
stages.marksNote: Not marked here; planning is credited in coursework

points: Artefact B must be a piece you can fully finish in 5 hours. Choose a medium and size suited to that, and different from Artefact A (two distinctly different areas of practice).
Use your Artefact B pages in the journal (Exploration, Development Sheets 1 and 2) to settle your idea, composition, colours, materials and steps. Those pages are marked in the coursework component.
Test the techniques you will use in your development sheets, so there are no surprises on the day.
Write a time plan for the two sessions. Know what must be done by the end of the first 2.5 hours.

stages.name: Rules and kit for the day
stages.marksNote: Not marked, but breaking the rules can lose marks

points: You make Artefact B from scratch. You may not use any prepared materials: paper must be blank, and you cannot make any part in advance. You cannot bring in raw footage or imagery to edit.
Materials and equipment come from your school. Agree the list with your teacher so everything is there on the day.
You get your Visual Journal back for reference and you may work into it if needed to realise Artefact B.
If your artefact needs a still life, you may bring in inanimate primary sources of a reasonable size. No other visual aids are allowed.
No internet access.
Artefact B must be completely finished, dry and ready for secure storage at the end of the 5 hours. There is no drying time afterwards, so wet clay wrapped in plastic is not admissible.
2D work must not be framed, and 3D work must not be wrapped or boxed.
At the end you receive a tamper-evident envelope for the journal, Artefact A and any 2D Artefact B or MP4. 3D work goes on top. Put your label on each artefact.

stages.name: First 2.5 hours: set up and build

guide.h: Use the first session to commit
points: Start with your journal page open. Set up your composition or structure quickly: major shapes, proportions, layout.
Get the whole piece blocked in or constructed by the break, so you are refining, not starting, in the second session.
Criterion F (30 marks): a personal and meaningful artefact that realises your intentions and communicates the ideas in the journal. Bands 0 to 12, 13 to 23, 24 to 30.
Criterion G (20 marks): your understanding of art elements and design principles. Decide on your focal point, contrast, balance and use of colour now. Bands 0 to 8, 9 to 15, 16 to 20.
Use the break to look at the piece from a distance and write down the three things that most need to change in the second session.

stages.name: Second 2.5 hours: refine and finish
stages.marksNote: Criteria H, I and J, 50 marks

points: Criterion H (30 marks): your knowledge of media, materials and techniques. Show control of the materials you tested in your journal. Bands 0 to 12, 13 to 23, 24 to 30.
Criterion I (10 marks): overall impact. Step back and check the artwork as a whole. Bands 0 to 4, 5 to 7, 8 to 10.
Criterion J (10 marks): Artefact B should be in a different area of practice from Artefact A, using different materials and techniques.
Leave the last 15 minutes for finishing details, labelling and checking it is dry and ready to store.
Stop on time. Unfinished work loses marks under F and H, since the artefact has to realise your intentions.

stages.name: How the 100 marks are marked
stages.marksNote: Bands, grade descriptors and Ordinary Level conversion

points: The 100 marks are Artefact B's realised work: F 30, G 20, H 30, I 10 and J 10. The examiner views the journal and both artefacts as a whole project.
Reference marks: Higher Level grades are H1 at 90 to 100, H2 80 to 89, H3 70 to 79, H4 60 to 69, H5 50 to 59, H6 40 to 49, H7 30 to 39 (2025 scheme).
Ordinary Level: a reference mark of 60 or more is 100 marks, 30 to 59 gets 40 added, and 1 to 29 is doubled plus 10.
The scheme asks for 'perseverance, creativity and imagination, focus and relevance', strong drawing, good use of primary sources, art elements and design principles, and understanding of media.
The examiner looks at the journal first, then Artefact B, so make sure your artefact visibly grows out of your Artefact B development sheets.

criteria.name: F: Personal and meaningful artefact
criteria.whatTopMarksLook: Realises intentions, shows visual language and aesthetics, and communicates the ideas in the journal (24 to 30).

criteria.name: G: Art elements and design principles
criteria.whatTopMarksLook: Individual response showing knowledge and understanding of elements and principles (16 to 20).

criteria.name: H: Media, materials and techniques
criteria.whatTopMarksLook: Individual response showing knowledge and understanding of your chosen media, materials and techniques (24 to 30).

criteria.name: I: Overall impact
criteria.whatTopMarksLook: The overall impact of the finished artefact (8 to 10).

criteria.name: J: Two areas of practice
criteria.whatTopMarksLook: Realised through a different area of practice from Artefact A, with different materials and techniques (8 to 10).

rules: 5 hours on a single day, in two periods of 2.5 hours with a break (2026 brief).
Artefact B is made from scratch. No prepared materials and no raw footage or imagery.
Your Visual Journal is available for reference and you can work into it if needed.
Only inanimate primary sources of reasonable size may be brought in, such as a still life. No other visual aids and no internet.
Artefact B must be dry and ready for storage at the end. No drying time is given.
The work must be Artefact B's pages in the journal and the artefact must match them.
The practical exam is 100 of the 350 practical marks (20% of the Art grade).
mistakes: Choosing a medium that cannot dry, set or finish in 5 hours.
Making Artefact B in the same area of practice as Artefact A.
Bringing in pre-made materials, printed images for editing, or a pre-primed canvas. The paper must start blank.
Leaving the final hour for the biggest part of the work. Block in the whole piece before the break.
Ignoring your journal plan on the day. Examiners view it as one project.
Not labelling the artefact with your examination number.

conflicts: The 2026 brief says the coursework period is normally 12 school weeks starting in January, but 2026 candidates got the brief on 28 November 2025 because of adjusted arrangements. The 2027 brief and dates are not yet published, so 2026 dates are given as a guide only.

In 2026 the Final Proposal and Artist's Statement pages were issued but earned no marks, and candidates did not need to complete the whole Visual Journal. The 2025 marking scheme lists only the Exploration page and Development Sheets 1 and 2 for each artefact. Whether 2027 keeps these adjustments is not confirmed, so do the pages anyway: they help your planning.

The NCCA specification says the practical examination is 'within 5 hours of a single day'. The 2026 brief adds that it is split into two 2.5 hour periods with a break. The brief is the more recent and detailed source and is used here.
